description: Tray monitor for AI coding-agent token usage, cost, and subscription quota. Windows port of TokenBar.
notes: Syrtis is managed by Scoop here, not by its own installer. Update it with
In 0.3.0 the in-app 'Check for updates' button reports a failure on a Scoop
install. Nothing is wrong and nothing is broken: that build has no way to
tell 'someone else manages this copy' apart from 'the check failed'. A later
release says so plainly instead. Either way, the button is not the update
Usage data lives in %APPDATA%\tokscale and %LOCALAPPDATA%\TokenBar, outside
the Scoop directory, so it survives updates and is left behind on uninstall.
pre_uninstall: # Launch at login is two registry values that must agree: the Run command,
# and a StartupApproved\Run record whose absence means enabled and whose odd
# first byte means Task Manager disabled it. That contract lives in
# src/TokenBar.App/AutostartService.cs.
# This hook deliberately does NOT reimplement it. It snapshots both values
# verbatim and post_install puts both back verbatim. Nothing here interprets
# them, so nothing here can drift when that C# changes - two earlier versions
# of this hook each carried over part of the contract and silently corrupted
# the user's setting in a different way.
# Why it must delete at all: only the Velopack uninstaller clears the Run
# entry (Program.cs OnBeforeUninstallFastCallback), and an extraction install
# never runs it, so uninstalling would leave a startup command pointing into
# a deleted directory.
# Why it must restore: scoop update runs this hook too - scoop-update.ps1
# calls Invoke-HookScript 'pre_uninstall' with the old manifest before
# installing the replacement - and the hook is given nothing that
# distinguishes an update from a removal.
# Conditional on the Run value living under this app's Scoop directory: the
# same machine may also hold a Velopack install that legitimately owns these
# values, and touching those would break its launch at login.
try {
$appRoot = Split-Path $dir -Parent
$run = 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'
$approved = 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run'
$command = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $run -Name 'Syrtis' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).'Syrtis'
if ($command -and $command.Trim('"').StartsWith($appRoot, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
$record = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $approved -Name 'Syrtis' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).'Syrtis'
$snapshot = @{ command = $command; approved = $(if ($record) { [Convert]::ToBase64String([byte[]]$record) } else { $null }) }
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'syrtis-autostart.restore') -Value ($snapshot | ConvertTo-Json -Compress) -Encoding UTF8
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $run -Name 'Syrtis' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $approved -Name 'Syrtis' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
} catch { }
post_install: # Puts back exactly what pre_uninstall snapshotted, including the absence of
# the StartupApproved record - a missing record means enabled, so restoring
# only the command would silently re-enable a startup the user had turned off
# Nothing to do on a first install: the marker only exists if this app's own
# pre_uninstall wrote it moments earlier. The age check is what keeps a final
# uninstall final - a marker left by a real removal would otherwise sit in
# TEMP and re-enable launch at login on an unrelated install later. Scoop runs
# the uninstall and install phases of an update back to back.
Write-Host 'Restored the launch-at-login state across the update.'
